Commentary.Commentary: Right then, that's all we have from this exciting match. South Africa were in early pressure but bounced back superbly and ended up with a convincing win. The action now shifts to the Mangaung Oval, Bloemfontein for the second ODI on the 4th of March. Do join us at 1300 local (1100 GMT). Cheers!

South African skipper, Quinton de Kock, says that he is pleased with the way his boys went about it today. Lauds Klaasen for his knock and praises Ngidi for the way he bowled. Adds that they knew they had hitters down the order and it was just a matter of staying there and being consistent in what they do. Shares that Ngidi has a knack of picking wickets and he is enjoying his leadership role. On his role as an opener/keeper/captain, de Kock replies that he has always felt that his keeping helps him in captaincy and he feels it won't be the same if he goes out in the outfield. Signs off by saying that he is still feeling fresh and good!

Australian skipper, Aaron Finch, says that it was a good start by his bowlers but Klaasen and Miller batted superbly. Admits that they lost wickets pretty consistently and that cost them the match. Tells that they got outplayed in all the disciplines and South Africa were the better side. Mentions that you expect nothing less from the Proteas and hopes to bounce back in the second game.

HEINRICH KLAASEN IS THE MAN OF THE MATCH! Says that it's a great feeling and that's why that celebration came off. Adds that the last year and a half have been tough for him and he is relieved with today's performance. Mentions that it felt like another comeback and he just stuck to the game plan and is happy to perform for the team. Praises David Miller for his knock which took the pressure off him. States that they just needed to bat deep and bat with low risk. Further says that David Miller allowed him to play his natural game and then he unleashed a little more.

Earlier in the day, South Africa opted to bat but found themselves in troubled waters after losing three quick wickets. But Heinrich Klaasen dug in deep and put on a great show with the bat. His partnerships with Kyle Verreynne and David Miller bailed the African team out and they managed to post a very challenging total on the board. In defense, the bowlers turned up to tighten the noose and it was a complete bowling performance by them. A near clinical win to take a 1-0 lead in the series. Stay tuned for the presentation...

Steven Smith fought a brave battle for Australia. Till the time he was in the middle, Australia had hope. He constructed a couple of stands and was laying the platform for an onslaught in the death overs. However, the period when Mitchell Marsh and Smith departed in consecutive overs hurt their chances badly. Post that, there was very little fight shown by the Kangaroos and they succumbed to a heavy defeat.

A very efficient defense from South Africa! They bowled according to the plan and stuck to the basics. After dismissing the Aussie openers fairly cheaply, there was a partnership that blossomed between Steven Smith and Marnus Labuschagne but the Protea bowlers didn't lose hope. They held their nerves and concentrated on drying out the boundaries. This can be substantiated by the fact that it took Australia 18 overs to hit their first boundary after Powerplay 1.

OUT! TIMBER! That is the end of the match! SOUTH AFRICA WIN BY 74 RUNS! It is on a length and around off, Hazlewood is beaten for sheer pace and fails to keep it out. The stumps light up and it's lights out for Australia.
FOUR! Good shot! It is short and around middle, Zampa waits for it and then pulls it nicely over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Outside off, this is slapped towards mid off for one.
One more play and a miss! Outside off again. Hazlewood goes after it but fails to put bat on ball.
Outside off, fuller in length. Hazlewood goes for it but misses.
On a length and around middle, this is pushed down to long on for one.
Josh Hazlewood is the number 11 batsman.

OUT! CAUGHT! Another spectacular catch from Verreynne. It is a slower one and on middle, Cummins swings but only manages to hit it high up in the air towards long on. KV runs in and takes an excellent catch with a dive forward.
Out comes the sweep shot. It is hit through mid-wicket for one.
Zampa plays the reverse sweep. It is hit towards backward point where the fielder dives to his right and saves a run.
A little too short! Cummins pulls it behind square on the leg side for one.
Malan is now seen walking back! He is holding his hamstring and is in a lot of pain. Not good, not a debut to remember.
Nicely played! On the pads, this is swept towards fine leg for one.
On leg stump, it turns back in. Zampa looks to flick but misses to get hit on the pads. A huge shout but not given.
Adam Zampa is in next.
OUT! That is probably the last nail in the coffin for Australia! Short looks to take on Shamsi. He steps out but Shamsi shortens the length. Short swings but misses and de Kock does the rest.
One more dot! A slower one, Cummins swings again but it goes off the inner half towards mid-wicket. Just a boundary and a wicket from the over. Brilliant.
FOUR! Much, much-needed! Australia though need a lot more. This is full and it is a slower one. Cummins smashes it over the bowler's head and bags a boundary.
On off, Cummins works it towards mid-wicket.
Length and on off, it is guided to point.
Pat Cummins arrives in the middle with the asking rate 11.6.

OUT! RUN OUT! Number 7 down and Starc's struggle comes to an end! One more slower one outside off, Starc once again looks to cut but gets a bottom edge. He comes out of the crease in search of a run but is sent back. The keeper picks up the ball up and hits the bull's eye at the striker's end. Starc is well short of his crease!
A slower one outside off, Starc slashes but misses. Clever bowling. Starc probably just needs to give the strike over to Short. Dots are something they can't afford at the moment.
Direct hit and it would have been tight! Full, very full and on middle, this is hit towards cover. A single taken.
Another dot! On off, Starc looks to play the slog sweep but it goes off the inner half towards mid-wicket.
Another single! On the shorter side and around off, it is slapped towards cover for one.
Very full and on middle, Short jams it back to the bowler.
On middle, this is hit down to long off for one.

That is a nasty blow! Miller seems fine though. Flatter and on off, it is pushed towards short cover. Miller there gets some bad bounce off the practice pitch and it hits him on the face. David stands there and checks his mouth. All teeth in place. Good to carry on.
Full and wide outside off, Starc reaches out for it but only manages a bottom edge towards the leg side. One taken.
A short ball on middle, Short pulls it through square leg and takes one.
One more short ball outside off, Starc reaches out for it. He ends up bottom edging it towards point for one.
Full and wide outside off, Starc again goes after it but misses.
Outside off, Starc swings but misses.
Length and around off, Starc pushes it to mid off.
Powerplay 3 begins! A maximum of 5 fielders are now allowed outside the ring till the end.
On the shorter side and outside off, it is pushed through covers for one.
One more single as Short slaps it through covers. Singles won't do it for the visitors. They need boundaries.
Mitchell Starc walks out to bat.

OUT! In the air... taken! Shamsi does pick one and it is a big wicket of Carey. The pressure of the run rate creeping up gets the better of Carey. This is tossed up on off, Carey looks to go downtown as he tries to clear long off. Does not time it that well and Miller takes an easy catch in the deep. It now looks an impossible task for Australia. 97 needed in 62.
Shortish again and around off, Carey looks to cut but ends up bottom edging it towards cover.
Just a single! Shorter again and around off, it is slapped through covers for one more.
Shorter in length and outside off, Short slaps it to covers. Runs needed per over above 9.
Tabraiz Shamsi is back on. He has three overs up his sleeves. So far has gone for 5-an-over without a wicket. Can he pick up a few here and close this chase?
On the pads, Short works it nicely through mid-wicket and takes one. Tidy from AP. 98 needed in 66 balls.
A dot! Shorter and around off, Short looks to cut but mistimes it towards covers.
A quick run! On a length and around off, Carey drops it towards cover and takes one. Runs needed below 100 now.
Length and it is another slower one on middle, D'Arcy pushes it past the bowler for one.
Slower one on off, it is guided to the man at point.
Angled into the pads, Carey works it behind square on the leg side and takes one.
A dot to end! Full and on middle, this is hit back towards Ngidi. End of another good over by Ngidi.

Overthrow! A couple! On middle, this is worked towards mid on. A single is taken. The fielder has a shy at the bowler's end but misses. The fielder backing up lets it through and another run is taken.
Length and around off, Short guides it towards the man at point.
A slower one outside off, Short looks to drive it on the off side but it goes off the inner half back towards the bowler.
Back of a length again, Carey opens the face of the bat and guides it down to third man for one.
Back of a length and on off, this is guided towards point.
FOUR! Lovely shot! One which will release the pressure a little. Good end to the over. It is fuller and around middle, Short lofts it over mid on and bags a boundary.
Full again and on off, Carey jams it out through covers and takes one.
On the fuller side, Short hits it hard through covers and takes one.
On off, Short pushes it back to the bowler.
Back of a length and on off, Carey pushes it towards cover. He takes a run. The fielder has a shy at the striker's end but misses. Carey wants another but then is sent back.
Short and on the body, Short pulls it down to fine leg and takes one.
Bowling change. Andile Phehlukwayo (5-0-27-0) is back for another spell. Nortje bowled well from this end in his previous spell and Andile would look to maintain the same pressure.
Another dot to end! Just the single from the over. 113 now needed in 84. This is angled into the pads, Carey works it towards mid-wicket.
One more dot! Very full and on middle, it is hit back to the bowler.
Attacks the stumps, Carey stays back and keeps it out.
A high full toss, Carey is taken by surprise. He pushes it back to the bowler.
Length and around off, Carey pushes it towards the fielder at cover.
Up and over! Fuller and around off, Short lofts it over covers and takes one.
Down the leg side, Short looks to flick but misses. Wided.
Back of a length and on off, Carey guides it to point. End of a successful over for the hosts.
On the shorter side and on middle, Short pulls it through square leg and a single is taken.
A swing a miss! Outside off, Short goes after it but misses it.
Shorter and around off, Short gets off the mark as he pushes it nicely through covers for two.
Good length and on off, it is kept out.
D'Arcy Short walks out to bat now. The last recognized batter in this side is in the middle now. The onus will be on this pair to see the side home.

OUT! LBW! Is that the game for South Africa? Well, two set batters back in the hut and with still another 118 runs needed, you have to feel so. Nortje lands this on a length and around middle, it skids through after pitching. Smith looks to flick but misses. It hits the pad, a huge appeal goes up and so does the finger. Smith does have a chat with Carey but then starts walking back. He is very disappointed with himself. This game has changed in the course of two overs here. Ball Tracker shows it to be hitting the leg pole.
Ohh! Ngidi hits the deck hard on off and middle, Carey looks to tap it on the off side but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Good length ball on off, Carey starts his innings with a solid back foot defense.
Alex Carey walks out to bat.

OUT! Bowled! Ngidi comes and strikes again. It is a gem of a delivery from Lungi and Marsh is completely outdone by it. The budding stand comes to an end. The all-in-all destructor in this Australian batting line-up is out of here. Good length delivery outside off, Marsh looks to drive it on the up but the ball tails back in and goes right between the gate of bat and pad to disturb the off pole. Marsh had a chance to silence his critics but unfortunately he fails to do so. Australia need another 118 in 98 balls.
Follows the boundary with a single towards cover.
FOUR! Horrible ball from  Ngidi and treated with disdain by Smith. Juicy full toss on off, Smith slams it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Good length ball on off, Smith gets on his back foot and plays a very good looking punch but straight to the man at cover.
Lungi Ngidi is back on! 5-0-20-2, his numbers so far.
A single to end! So despite going for a boundary, just the 7 from it. Full and on off, it is hit to mid on for one. 123 needed in 17 overs.
Very well bowled! A yorker at 148 kph. Smith does well to get his bat down and jam it out.
Fuller and on middle, looking to hit the pads of Smith. He works it to mid-wicket.
Fuller and wide outside off, Marsh carves it through cover-point for one.
A single now! Shorter and around off, Smith slashes, it goes off the outside edge down to third man.

FOUR! 'Oh no' is what Smith shouted when he played the shot. Perhaps he thought he had chipped one straight to mid off. Luckily for him, it goes over the fielder. Rare, very rare misjudgement from him! Fuller and off, Smith looks to go over mid off. Does not hit it that well but gets enough to clear mid off. A boundary to begin the over.
Another single! On off, fuller, it is chipped down to long off for a single. 7 from the over with no risk taken.
On middle, it is worked through square leg for one more.
On middle, it is worked through mid-wicket for one.

Two runs! On the pads, Smith flicks it over square leg. He takes one and goes for the second. The throw is towards the keeper who whips the bails off but Smith makes in nicely with a full length dive.
On middle, it is worked through mid-wicket for one.
On middle, Smith works it uppishly but well short of deep mid-wicket for one.
On the pads, Smith looks to flick but misses, it hits the pads and rolls on the leg side. A leg bye taken.
On a length and around off, Marsh guides it through backward point for one.
On the shorter side and outside off, Smith guides it through point for one.
Angled into the batter, Smith looks to flick but closes the face of the bat early. He gets a soft leading edge to covers.
Back of a length and on off, Smith pushes it wide of covers and takes an easy two.
Slightly shorter and outside off, the ball skids through. Smith is late in the cut shot. Beaten. Good start by Nortje.
Anrich Nortje is back on. He has not had a good day with the ball so far. 25 from his 4 overs in his first spell.
One more single to end the over which also brings up 150 for Australia! On middle, it is pushed back to the left of the bowler who dives but only gets a hand to it. It rolls down to long off for one.
A low full toss on middle, Marsh strokes it towards covers for one.

A huge, huge shout but it is doing too much! This is on middle, it turns back in sharply. Marsh looks to defend but misses to get hit on the pads. A huge shout from the bowler as he charges towards the striker's end. Nothing doing as far as the umpire is concerned. Spinning too much and would have easily missed leg.
On middle, Marsh stays leg side of the delivery and pushes it to covers.
Loopy ball on middle, Smith works it through mid-wicket for one.
On the shorter side, this is cut through point for one.
A single to end Maharaj's spell! A good outing for him. His figures read 10-0-48-1. His last ball is on off, Marsh pushes it through covers for one.
Flatter and quicker on middle, Marsh pushes it back to the bowler.
Tossed up on off again, Smith eases it down to long off for one.
Floats it on middle, it is pushed back to the bowler.
On off, Marsh pushes it through cover-point for one.
Misfield and a run! On middle, this is pushed towards short mid-wicket who dives over the ball and it goes down to long on for one.

FOUR! Welcome boundary for the Aussies. Their first one since the end of Powerplay 1. Flighted on middle and leg, Marsh makes room and drives it with ease through mid off for a boundary. This would calm the nerves for Mitchell Marsh.
Short again from Shamsi. Marsh glances it to the right of long on and gets a couple.
Tossed up on middle, Smith nudges it towards long on for a single.
Googly on off, Marsh half-checks his drive towards mid off and gets a single.
Flighted on leg, Marsh goes on his back foot and flicks it towards square leg.
Floated on middle, Marsh tucks it towards mid-wicket.
On middle, Marsh is off the mark as he pushes it down to long on and takes one. End of a successful over from Maharaj.
Flatter and on middle, kept out.
Mitchell Marsh is the new man in in.

OUT! Labuschagne holes out! He has literally thrown his wicket away. A nothing shot from him here. Maharaj is successful in breaking the stand. This is tossed up on middle and off, Labuschagne plants his front foot forward and ends up chipping it straight down the throat of Ngidi who makes no mistake at long on. A good little innings from Labuschagne comes to an end but he needed to stay out there longer. South Africa will now look to build more pressure on the Aussies. They are just ahead in the game at the moment. 159 more needed.
Flatter and on off, it is pushed through covers for one.

Just wide! Fifty up for Smith! Once again he has taken the responsibility of pulling the Aussies out of trouble. He needs to continue though. However, he must have had his heart in his mouth on this delivery. It is angled into the pads, Smith looks to flick but gets a leading edge. It goes just wide of the diving Maharaj and down towards long on for one. Two taken.
Flatter and around off, Labuschagne goes back and pushes it through covers for one. A risky shot, he had no room to play with but still managed to stroke it through covers.
A dot to end! Just 4 runs from the over. On the pads, Smith looks to flick but misses. It hits the pads and de Kock does the rest.
On the pads, Smith works it to square leg.
Clever shot for two! On middle, Smith chips it nonchalantly over the bowler's head and takes two.
Just wide! The dot balls almost paid off! This is tossed up on middle, Labuschagne goes a little hard at it. He hits it uppishly but wide of mid-wicket and down to long on for one.
Very full and on off, Labuschagne can't beat mid off.
Gives it a lot of flight and lands it on middle, Smith works it through mid-wicket for one.
Floated on middle and off, Marnus keeps it out. 167 needed off 150 balls at the halfway stage of this chase.
Uppish but safe. Shorter on middle and off, Labuschagne pulls it wide of mid-wicket and gets a couple.
Tossed up on off, Smith eases it to long off and rotates the strike.
Floated on the stumps, Labuschagne milks it to long on and rotates the strike.
Shorter on middle, Smith punches it to long on and gets to the other end.

Darted on the pads, Labuschagne flicks it to the right of square leg. Phehlukwayo at square leg anticipated it to go towards mid-wicket and hence he went that way initially but he manages to clean it up before the ropes. Three taken by the batters.
A single to end! Shamsi is really doing a good job here. Just the two from this over. On middle, this is pushed down to long on for one.

Stumping chance goes abegging! It is very full and on the pads, Labuschagne looks to whip it but the ball hits the pad and goes behind towards de Kock. ML drags his foot out but luckily for him, de Kock does not collect it. Not easy for the South African skipper as it came to him after hitting the pad.
Just a single now! On off, Smith drags it towards long on and gets to the other end.
Gets away with a full toss! It is on middle, Smith hits it back to the bowler. Good pressure building here.
On middle again, Smith once again works it towards square leg. Very good field placement. They have two fielders there so a single is stopped. Smith will have to try something else.
On middle, Smith works it towards square leg. He thinks of a run but is sent back.
Quicker one, it's fired on middle, Smith helps it to square leg for a single. Quiet going from the Aussies, the RRR is touching 7 now.
Loopy and full around off, Labuschagne drives it with the spin through mid off for a run.
Floated and full on middle, Marnus leans forward and defends it on the leg side.
Flatter and shorter ball on middle, Smith covers the line and forces it to long on for one.
Turns it off his pads towards the square leg umpire and scampers across to the other end.
Tossed up ball on middle, Labuschagne wants to flick it from the crease but closes the face of the bat early. Ends up pushing it back.
Nicely played! Plays the paddle sweep, takes it on the full and hits it towards fine leg for one. Another good over by Shamsi.
Close! Looks to bring out the sweep but it is a little too full. The ball goes off the inner half towards square leg. Shamsi has some words for the batters, Labuschagne has no reaction though.
Good captaincy! De Kock brings in a square leg to stop a run! Labuschagne works it exactly to that fielder.
On the pads, Smith works it around the corner and gets to the other end.
Good stop! This is given a lot of flight and it lands on off, Smith hits it hard back to the right of the bowler who makes a good stop.
Good running! On middle, Smith waits and then works it through square leg. Takes two with ease.
5 singles from the over then! Outside off, Smith waits for it and then guides it through point. He retains strike.
One more single! Labuschagne this time pushes this ball on off down to long off.
The arm ball, it is on off, ML guides it to point.
One more single as this is eased down to long on.
Shorter in length again, Labuschagne goes back and punches it down to long off for one.
Slightly shorter and around off, Smith pushes it through covers. Calls for two but it is too close to the fielder and only a single.
Full and flighted on off, it's pushed back to the bowler as Smith reacts to drag his bat inside the crease at the non-striker's end. 6 from Shamsi's first over!
Mishit! Too full in length around off, Labuschagne tries to sweep but ends up under edging it to the left of leg slip.
Wide! Skidding down the leg side, Marnus tries his best to get some bat behind it but misses.
Tickles a full ball in the gap on the leg side and picks up a single.
Spinning into the batsman from around middle and leg, Smith eases it past leg slip and collects a couple of runs. 50-run stand comes up and also Australia have reached 100!
Shorter and spinning in on the pads, Labuschagne pulls it fine down the leg side and gets to the other end.
Shamsi starts with a slower leg spinner on middle and off, Smith flicks it to the leg side for a single.
Tabraiz Shamsi is introduced into the attack for the first time today.
This time Smith punches it through covers and retains the strike.

Uppish but safe. Flighted and slower on off, Smith thinks it is there to drive but the ball is slow to come onto him and he hits it uppishly. Luckily for him and the tourists, it falls well short of the fielder.
Shorter on middle, Labuschagne punches it towards long off for a run.
Quicker on middle and leg now. Labuschagne flicks it but finds short mid-wicket.
Shorter and slower, turning away from Smith. He drives it uppishly towards cover for a single.
Floated on off, Labuschagne milks it towards long off for a single.
Back of a length around off, Marnus pulls it towards deep mid-wicket and gets a single. 200 more required in 192 balls.
WIDE! Slower ball wide outside off. Too wide and Labuschagne leaves it alone. The umpire wides it.
Slower ball outside off, Smith punches it right off the meat but there is a man there in the deep so just one.
On the pads, Labuschagne whips it in front of square and eases down to the other end.
Nice change of pace from the Protea bowler. Slower ball outside off, Labuschagne looks to drive but misses.
Outside off on a length, Smith cuts it hard but close to the point fielder. Bavuma dives to his right and takes the pace off the ball. He fails to collect it and that allows them to take a run.
Length ball just outside off, Smith whips it towards mid-wicket.
Darted on the pads, SS glances it to the leg side and keeps the strike.
Flighted on middle, Labuschagne milks it towards long on and gets to the other end.
Shorter on middle and leg, Labuschagne tucks it to the leg side.
Tossed up on middle, Smith nudges it towards mid on and rotates the strike.
Flighted on middle, Smith taps it to the right of the bowler on the bounce.
Floated on the pads, Labuschagne flicks it towards mid-wicket and gets to the other end.
Good length ball outside off, Labuschagne runs it down towards third man and keeps the strike.
Fuller on off and middle, Steven flicks it to the leg side and gets a single.
On off and middle, Smith plays it to mid-wicket.
Length delivery around off, Smith hangs on his back foot and drags his pull behind square on the leg side and gets a couple.
Good length ball on off, Smith strokes it to the left of mid on and shouts a loud wait to his partner.
Play and a miss. Fuller delivery outside off, Smith looks to drive it through covers but misses.

Was that pad or bat? Not sure! This is floated up on the pads, Labuschagne looks to work it against the turn but misses the line. It seems to have hit the pad and lobbed on the off side. Another tidy over.

In the air... wide! A risky shot that from Smith! He comes down the track but does not get to the pitch of the ball. He looks to whip it against the turn but gets a leading edge. It lands safe, away from the fielder at short covers for one.
Slightly shorter and around middle, it is pushed down to long on for one more single.
Loopy ball and on off, this is eased down to long off for an easy run.

Had the short mid-wicket fielder stopped that, it could have been close. On middle, this is worked towards mid-wicket. The batters set off. The fielder dives but does not stop it cleanly. A quick single.
Flatter and on middle, it is pushed back towards the bowler who collides with the non-striker and fails to stop it. Good sportsmanship from Smith as he does not take a run.
Keshav Maharaj is back into the attack now! A slip in place for him.
A dot to end! On middle, Smith strokes it to mid on. A tidy over from Phehlukwayo.
On the shorter side and on the body, Labuschagne pulls it down to fine leg and gets to the other end.
One more length delivery around off, Smith, just like ML did last ball, plays it late and down to third man for one.
Width on offer and outside off, Labuschagne waits for it and then guides it down to third man. Gets off strike.
On the stumps, Smith at the end, works it towards mid-wicket where the fielder dives to his right and makes a good stop. Can't stop the single though.
Length and around off, it is pushed back to the bowler.
Ngidi is seen walking off the field! Maybe to get a refreshment.
Outside off, just behind a driving length. Labuschagne looks to drive but it goes off the inner half on the leg side.
Full and outside off, Smith strokes it through covers and another single results.
A single now as a length delivery outside off is pushed through covers.
On middle, Labuschagne works it through mid-wicket. He beats the fielder there and takes two.
This is angled into the batter, Smith works it with the angle through mid-wicket for one.
A muted appeal! A length ball is pushed back to the bowler. Ngidi underarms it onto the stumps and appeals but Smith is well in.
Landed outside off, chopped down through the vacant slip region towards third man for a couple.
Landed outside off, dabbed to third man for one.
Short and outside off, cut through point but it is stopped well.
Down the leg side, flicked away for a run.
Short and outside off, cut uppishly but behind point for a single.

NOT OUT. Close? Yes. Close in hitting the 6th stump down the leg side. Poor de Kock. Blindly trusted his bowler. Did not use his own judgement. A length ball, down the leg side, Smith missed his flick and was hit on the pads. Phehlukwayo appealed but the umpire moved away. The bowler as confident that was hitting the stumps and his captain went with him, without even waiting to think. Ball Tracker shows the impact itself to be outside leg. Review wasted.

Review time! South Africa reckon this is close. Smith got across slightly and missed his flick, getting hit on the pads. Seems to be missing leg. Oh dear. The impact itself is outside leg. Shocker of a review.
Outside off, played straight to point.
Around off, played straight to short mid-wicket.
Works this through the leg side for a run.
Outside off, steered towards third man for a single.

Big stare from Labuschagne to Ngidi, which is returned. A length ball around off, well defended. Ngidi collects and has a needless shy at the striker's end. Marnus did not like that. Especially when he did not move out of his crease.
Outside off, Smith looks to flick but misses. Gets hit on the pads and ekes out a leg bye.
POWERPLAY 2 time. 4 fielders allowed outside the 30-yard circle till the 40th over.

FOUR! Contrasting end to the over. A tight four balls, only to let it loose on the final two. Overpitched, outside off, Labuschagne leans and drives it through the covers! 58/2 for Australia in Powerplay 1, not far ahead from South Africa's 50/3.
FOUR! AUDACIOUS! Cannot really bowl there. Short and wide outside off, Labuschagne leaps and cuts it over cover. Off the mark in style.
Short and outside off, punched straight to cover.
Landed outside off, punched behind point for a single. 50 UP FOR AUSTRALIA. 242 more needed from 243 balls.
Outside off, punched off the back foot.
Play and a miss. Full and outside off, Smmith looks to drive but misses.
Andile Phehlukwayo into the attack as well.
Marnus Labuschagne walks in at number 4, replacing Warner.

OUT! CAUGHT! The third umpire has gone with the soft signal. Full and outside off, Warner pushes at this uppishly. The ball dips onto Kyle Verreyne at cover-point who dives forward, takes the catch and claims it. But Warner stands his ground. The Proteas are confident and the umpires get to confer. They refer it upstairs with the soft signal as out. The first replay seems to indicate that the ball has gone into the palms, with the fingers underneath the ball. But the more you look at it, the more you feel it has bounced. Eventually, OUT flashes on the giant screen. Both the openers dismissed inside Powerplay 1. 243 more needed from 246 balls.

Is that a legal catch? South Africa are celebrating. But David Warner is going nowhere. The umpires get together now. The soft signal is... OUT. So the third umpire needs clear evidence to overturn that. Seems like it has gone into the palm with the fingers underneath the ball. Looks a clean catch. And given.
Another slower ball, this time Smith gets across and works it with soft hands towards mid on for a quick single. The pressure is on the fielder, Janneman Malan and he fumbles.
Slower ball, pushed straight to mid on.
Outside off, on a length, punched straight to cover.
Good running. Warner just taps it towards mid off with soft hands and the single is completed with ease.
Full and around off, pushed straight to mid off with a loud call of 'WAIT ON!'
WIDE. Down the leg side, tuck shot missed.
On middle, tucked wide of mid-wicket for a couple. Smith moves to 11 from 12 balls.
Outside off, punched straight to cover.

FOUR! The new bat comes into use straightaway. A short ball, around off, extra bounce, but Smith rides it well. Gets across, watches the bouncer well and plays his shot with control, rolling his wrists on the shot. Gets it along the ground, past short fine leg. 248 more needed from 254 balls. The stand moves to 21 from 20 balls.
Change of bats for Smith.
A length ball outside off, coming in from around the wicket, calmly dabbed to third man for a run.
Full and outside off, driven towards mid on for a quick single.
Full and outside off, punched straight to cover.
And now, an ordinary effort. Full and outside off, Steven drives this straight to cover who gets a bad bounce, not quite getting his body behind the line and allows it to deflect behind. A run taken.
That is a fabulous stop. Full and outside off, Smith punches this on the up, though the covers but cannot get it past David Miller who dives to his left and stops the ball.
Full and down the leg side, Warner falls over in his attempt to flick and is hit on the pads. A leg bye stolen towards square leg.
A length ball outside off, Smith gets across and tucks it through square leg for a run.
Angling across, from leg to off, steered towards third man for a single.
Full and just around off, pushed back off the inner half towards mid on.
Around middle, helped through mid-wicket for a run.
Outside off, punched straight to cover.

FOUR! No stopping that. A short ball, around middle, Warner swivels and pulls it through square leg. There is deep mid-wicket in place but he cannot get there! 259 more needed from 266 balls. Warner moves to 21 from 18 balls. The stand is worth 10 from 8 deliveries.
Fuller and outside off, played with an open bat-face behind point for a single.
Around off, no room, coming in, well blocked.
A length ball outside off, punched straight to cover-point.
Outside off, punched straight to cover. 7 runs and a wicket from Ngidi's starter.
Appeal for LBW, but that is pitched outside leg. Turned down. Warner missed his flick.

EDGED, FOUR! Just a ball before, there was a slip in place. He would have gobbled this. He was moved to short extra cover. A length ball, outside off, getting it across the left-hander, Warner looks to steer it to third man but gets it off the outside edge, through the vacant first slip region, to the third man fence.
A cutter first ball to Smith, comes in from outside off, Steven helps it off the inner half through mid-wicket for a single.
Steven Smith walks in at number 3, replacing his skipper.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! There goes Finch. Ngidi takes just two balls to strike. A short ball, outside off, Finch backs away, trying to repeat his previous stroke but the extra pace and bounce on this ball induces an outside edge. Simple catch to his counterpart Quinton de Kock behind the stumps. 269 more needed to win from 274 balls.
On a length outside off, punched behind point. Good running effort from Tabraiz Shamsi to his right at third man. Two runs taken.
The Maharaj experimentation is done. Here is Lungi Ngidi.
A short ball, helped through square leg for another single.

That nipped back in off the seam. The Kryptonite for Finch. The indipper. On a length, outside off, Aaron looks to punch it through the off side but is cramped for room and gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
On a length, around off, angling away, dabbed to third man for one more.
A short ball, around middle, Warner looks to pull but mistimes it over mid-wicket. Two runs taken.
Around off, coming in, worked through mid-wicket for a run.
Landed outside off, steered towards third man for a single.
Outside off, punched wide of mid off for a run.

DROPPED! No reaction time. Outside off, Finch looks to run this down to third man but gets a bottom edge. Quinton de Kock is not even able to react by the time the ball hits his pads. Had he even realized, he could have taken it in the second attempt because the ball lobbed in the air, just behind him. A single taken.
Works this down the leg side for one.
Outside off, punched wide of mid off for a run.
FOUR! Nicely played. Full and outside off, Finch stays leg side of the ball, reaches out and lofts it beautifully over extra cover. The stand moves to 11 from 14 balls.
Around middle, tucked through mid-wicket for a single.
Full and outside off, driven but straight to short extra cover.
Back of a length outside off, Finch hops and pushes it towards point.
Full and outside off, tapped behind point for a single.
Around off, pushed towards cover again.
Around off, punched straight to cover.
FOUR! Finds the gap. On a length outside off, Warner punches this through the off side and gets it between backward point and cover-point. 287 more needed from 293 balls.
Anrich Nortje to bowl with the second new ball.
Arrowed in on the pads, tucked straight to short mid-wicket. Excellent start by Keshav Maharaj. Just a run from his opener.
Short and outside off, Finch backs away, looks to cut but mistimes it straight to short extra cover.
On the pads, helped through mid-wicket for the first run of the chase.
Fuller and around off, watchfully pushed back to the bowler.
Outside off, punched straight to cover.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.

We are back for the run chase. A cloudless sky awaits us. The Proteas get into a huddle. Out come the Aussie openers. Aaron Finch and David Warner. Oh. This is interesting. Spin straightaway. Keshav Maharaj to bowl with the first new ball. The aim is to take the pace off the ball against two power-hitters. Warner to face.
